# RoboDR vs Pulsar-only: attack scenarios

Pulsar source: `vendor/pulsar` at `4796504895ce42f95ffc1e414be19a5d7f40fc0a`; its `Receive` event carries `source, destination, len, is_tcp` (no payload). Events: FileCreated, FileDeleted, DirCreated, DirDeleted, FileOpened, FileLink, FileRename, ElfOpened, Fork, Exec, Exit, ChangeParent, CredentialsChange, Bind, Listen, Connect, Accept, Close, Receive, DnsQuery, DnsResponse, Send, Custom, Empty.

Attacker placements: **foreign** = a new host on the robot network (10.77.10.66); **insider** = the operator's own host (10.77.10.21), e.g. a compromised teleop laptop.

Each scenario runs alone in its own capture per placement, through its own robodr-agentd run, scored on its own spool: a RoboDR count is for that scenario only. A scenario counts as detected when one of its evidence ids (below; `EVIDENCE` in the script) fired in its own run; `crates/robodr-attack-sim/tests/agentd_e2e.rs` pins that for both placements and that none of these ids fire on the clean baseline. "own id missing" marks a run where the scenario's own expected id (`robodr-attack-sim list`) did not fire and the detection comes from another evidence id.

| Placement | Scenario | RoboDR (measured, rule id x count) | Pulsar-only best case (P1 unknown source, P2 short datagram) | What Pulsar-only cannot tell |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| foreign | rogue-participant | `robot.ros2.unknown_participant` x1 | P1 x3 of 171 datagrams received | that a DDS participant joined, its GUID, that it is not in the profile; from an allowed host nothing at all |
| foreign | guid-spray | `robot.ros2.discovery_flood` x11; `robot.ros2.unknown_participant` x8 | P1 x600 of 768 datagrams received | the number of distinct participants (all from one address); no rate rule exists in a per-event engine |
| foreign | malformed-rtps | `robot.rtps.malformed_discovery` x4; `robot.rtps.discovery_not_inspected` x20 | P1 x2296, P2 x190 of 2464 datagrams received | malformed RTPS of normal length (random bodies, bad submessage lengths, mutations, fragments) |
| foreign | cmd-vel-envelope | `robot.motion.linear_over_envelope` x95; `robot.firewall.rejected_over_hard_limit` x95 | **not visible** (identical addresses, ports and lengths) | anything: same host, port and length as the operator; the speed is in the payload |
| foreign | lowcmd-torque | `robot.unitree.legacy_unknown_sender` x1; `robot.motion.unprofiled_channel` x600; `robot.firewall.rejected_unknown_channel` x600 | **not visible** (frames go to the motor controller) | anything on the robot computer: the frames go to the motor controller; the torque is in the payload |
| insider | rogue-participant | `robot.ros2.unknown_participant` x1; `robot.ros2.identity_instances_exceeded` x1 | **nothing** of 171 datagrams received | that a DDS participant joined, its GUID, that it is not in the profile; from an allowed host nothing at all |
| insider | guid-spray | `robot.ros2.discovery_flood` x12; `robot.ros2.unknown_participant` x4 | **nothing** of 768 datagrams received | the number of distinct participants (all from one address); no rate rule exists in a per-event engine |
| insider | malformed-rtps | `robot.rtps.malformed_discovery` x4; `robot.rtps.discovery_not_inspected` x20 | P2 x190 of 2464 datagrams received | malformed RTPS of normal length (random bodies, bad submessage lengths, mutations, fragments) |
| insider | cmd-vel-envelope | `robot.motion.linear_over_envelope` x95; `robot.firewall.rejected_over_hard_limit` x95 | **not visible** (identical addresses, ports and lengths) | anything: same host, port and length as the operator; the speed is in the payload |
| insider | lowcmd-torque | `robot.motion.unprofiled_channel` x600; `robot.firewall.rejected_unknown_channel` x600 (own id missing) | **not visible** (frames go to the motor controller) | anything on the robot computer: the frames go to the motor controller; the torque is in the payload |

Detected: RoboDR 10/10, Pulsar-only best case 4/10 (a P1/P2 hit counts as detected, although it says only "a datagram from X" or "a short datagram", not what happened).

Where Pulsar-only is strong and RoboDR builds on it: host activity on the robot computer (shells, SROS 2 key reads, package installs, service tampering). RoboDR ships its rule pack for Pulsar (`rules/robodr/`, 86 rules) and correlates those host detections with the network ones (`robot.correlate.*`); those scenarios are not in this table (tools/e2e/redteam2.sh; they need Pulsar running on a real kernel, gap T27).
